hints: Focus on what each reagent actually reacts with, sodium is less selective than sodium carbonate.
Count for each molecule how many alcohol -OH groups and how many carboxylic acid -COOH groups it has.
Remember that 2 acidic protons give 1 mole of H2 with Na, but 2 carboxylic acids give 1 mole of CO2 with carbonate, then look for equal moles.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two different gas-forming reactions**

Sodium is a strong enough base to react with both alcohols and carboxylic acids to give hydrogen gas. Sodium carbonate is weaker and reacts only with carboxylic acids to give carbon dioxide gas.

$$2\text{ROH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RONa} + \text{H}_2$$
$$2\text{RCOOH} + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{RCOONa} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Turn functional groups into moles of gas**

For 1 mole of compound, moles of $\text{H}_2$ from Na = 0.5 x (total number of -OH from alcohols + -COOH). Moles of $\text{CO}_2$ from carbonate = 0.5 x (number of -COOH only).

So to get the same volume, the compound must have no alcohol groups, only carboxylic acid groups.

**Check each structure and conclude**

A has 2 alcohols, 0 acids. B has 1 alcohol, 1 acid. C has 1 alcohol, 0 acids. Only the ethanedioic acid structure with 2 $\text{-COOH}$ groups and no alcohol groups gives 1 mol $\text{H}_2$ and 1 mol $\text{CO}_2$.

$$\text{moles H}_2 = 0.5 \times 2 = 1, \quad \text{moles CO}_2 = 0.5 \times 2 = 1$$

options.A: This is ethane-1,2-diol, HOCH2CH2OH, with 2 alcohol groups. With Na it gives 1 mol H2, but with Na2CO3 it gives 0 mol CO2 because alcohols do not react with carbonate. Volumes are different.
options.B: This is 2-hydroxypropanoic acid (lactic acid) with 1 alcohol and 1 carboxylic acid. With Na it gives 1 mol H2 (0.5 + 0.5), but with carbonate it gives only 0.5 mol CO2 from the single -COOH. Volumes are different.
options.C: This is 2-hydroxyethanal, HOCH2CHO, with 1 alcohol and 1 aldehyde. With Na it gives 0.5 mol H2, but with carbonate it gives 0 mol CO2 because neither alcohol nor aldehyde reacts with carbonate. Volumes are different.
options.D: This is ethanedioic acid, HOOC-COOH, with 2 carboxylic acid groups and no alcohol groups. With Na: 2 acidic protons give 1 mol H2. With Na2CO3: 2 acids give 1 mol CO2. Both gases have the same moles and hence the same volume.
